solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pastry book with 50% off on cover

indicators.note: half the letters of the book's name are dropped, leaving only its first six

parts.note: Ecclesiastes is a book of the Old Testament
to cake something is to coat or cover it thickly, as with mud

explanation.surface: Someone sells a book at half price with a discount sticker on its jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with 50% off' keeps only the first half of the book's twelve-letter name; 'cover' looks like a book jacket but is a verb meaning to coat, and 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eccles cake is a small round British pastry filled with currants, named after a town near Manchester.

clue.text: Subdue prisoner with heartless eccentric

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: the central letter of the word for eccentric is removed

parts.note: queer in its old sense means odd or eccentric

explanation.surface: A jailer subdues an inmate who has a callous, odd character.
explanation.definitionFit: To conquer a foe is to defeat or subdue them; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Identify murder victim after tip from lab

indicators.note: the victim's name is placed after the single letter
the tip of a word is its first letter, taken here from the word lab

parts.note: Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis, the first murder victim

explanation.surface: Forensic scientists name a murder victim after a lead from the laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: To label something is to tag or identify it with a name.

clue.text: Gobstopper?

parts.note: read literally, something that stops what comes out of the gob, slang for mouth: a receptacle that catches spit

explanation.definitionFit: A spittoon is a bowl for spitting into, so in a playful sense it stops what leaves the mouth.

clue.text: Jet boat

parts.note: not a jet-propelled boat but a ship whose job is to carry jet planes

explanation.definitionFit: This naval vessel is a warship with a flight deck that carries and launches military jets.

clue.text: Recruit isn't let out without training, initially

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the two words are put out of order
without says a letter is taken away from the jumbled pool
initially picks the first letter of training

explanation.surface: A new soldier is refused leave until basic training is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ISNTLET, and 'without' plus 'training, initially' removes one T from those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To recruit someone, or to join up yourself, is to enlist in the armed forces.

clue.text: Resulting from fracas — boy's punishment?

indicators.note: the run of letters emerges from the end of fracas and the start of boy's

explanation.surface: A boy gets punished after a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO (anti-social behaviour order) was a British court order against nuisance conduct; the question mark admits it is a penalty only loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: This British court order restricting a troublemaker's behaviour served as a civil punishment.

clue.text: Market's to recommend restricting limits of private sector investment

indicators.note: the verb for recommend holds the other letters within it

parts.note: to advise is to recommend a course

indicators.note: here the limits are the closing letters of each of the three words

explanation.surface: An adviser urges curbs on private-sector investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits of' could mean both ends of each word, but only the final letters work; 'restricting' puts them inside the verb, and 'Market's' is the definition plus 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To market a product is to promote and advertise it to buyers.

clue.text: Source of blazing wood gathered by somebody?

definitions.text: Source of blazing wood gathered by somebody?

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter, taken from blazing
the tree is held inside the pronoun's letters

parts.note: one is a pronoun for some person
fir is a softwood tree and timber

explanation.surface: A heap of wood collected by someone becomes a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered by' places the tree inside the pronoun after its second letter; read whole, the clue also describes a heap of collected wood set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: A large outdoor fire is built from wood that people have collected into a pile.

clue.text: Hump, flipping hump

indicators.note: flipping turns the slang word over so it reads backwards

parts.note: hump and bonk are both British slang for having sex

explanation.surface: An exasperated person swears at a lump: 'Hump, flipping hump!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' also reads as a mild British swear word, hiding its reversal job.
explanation.definitionFit: A knob is a rounded lump or bump, so it can stand for a hump.

clue.text: I've learnt resistance, unfortunately, is immaterial

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone admits sadly that resisting has made no difference.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irrelevant has no bearing on the matter, so it is immaterial.

clue.text: Star's unfashionable hairstyle

definitions.meaning: in heraldry this word names a star with straight-edged points
a cut short at the front and long at the back, widely mocked

explanation.surface: A celebrity sports an outdated haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a five-pointed star in heraldry and the short-front, long-back haircut.

clue.text: Drunk tears round end of corridor in bar

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the single letter
drunk suggests the letters stagger into a new order
the end of corridor is its last letter

explanation.surface: A tipsy patron weeps at the end of a hallway inside a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' rearranges TEARS as RESTA, and 'round' wraps that around the corridor's last letter; 'bar' looks like a pub but is a verb meaning to hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone is to prevent or hold them back, the same as to restrain them.

clue.text: Cancel FT, for we managed to get hold of one

indicators.note: the jumbled letters surround the numeral
managed suggests the letters are handled and rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Financial Times staff fight to secure a copy before it is axed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges FTFORWE, and 'to get hold of' puts I inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To write off a debt or loss is to cancel it as unrecoverable.

clue.text: Bird changes colour

parts.note: to turn is to change, as leaves turn in autumn
a tone is a shade or colour

explanation.surface: A bird whose plumage alters hue with the season.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnstone is a wading shorebird that flips stones to find food.

clue.text: Object I bumped into when reversing

indicators.note: the verb for encountering is read backwards

parts.note: to bump into someone is to meet them by chance

explanation.surface: A driver backing up hits something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumped into' looks like a collision, but here it means meeting by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single thing or object, as in an item of furniture.

clue.text: Slowly burn top of strawberry crumble

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to moulder is to decay and crumble away

explanation.surface: A dessert recipe: brown the topping of a strawberry crumble gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumble' poses as a pudding but is a verb meaning to decay.
explanation.definitionFit: To smoulder is to burn slowly with smoke but no flame.

clue.text: Bass taken from river bank

indicators.note: the letter is removed from the river's name

parts.note: the Tiber is the river that flows through Rome
B is the abbreviation for bass in music

explanation.surface: An angler pulls a bass out of the water onto the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bass' and 'bank' both suggest fishing; the bank here is a row, not a river edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or level, as is a bank of seats or keys.

clue.text: I see grandmother's trapped, foolishly

indicators.note: the pair of pieces around it hold the relative inside

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire
nan is a familiar British word for grandmother

explanation.surface: Someone notices that granny has got herself stuck in a silly way.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop's 'see' is his diocese, here the cathedral city in Cambridgeshire; 'trapped' puts the relative between the first piece and the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting inanely means acting in a silly, senseless way, which is acting foolishly.

clue.text: Appear to have Mercedes stuck in traffic?

indicators.note: the car's short name is stuck inside the verb

parts.note: to come is to appear or arrive
Merc is the informal short name for a Mercedes car

explanation.surface: A Mercedes seems to be caught in a traffic jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' looks like road vehicles but here means trading.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic in goods means dealing or trade, which is commerce.

clue.text: Red setter outside home follows vehicle

indicators.note: the pronoun pair is placed after the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a road vehicle

indicators.note: the setter's pronoun goes around the word for home

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me
in means at home

explanation.surface: A red setter dog stands outside the house behind a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red setter' suggests the dog breed; the setter is the puzzle's author, ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmine is a vivid crimson, a shade of red.

clue.text: Deposit penny on mantelpiece

parts.note: a mantelpiece is a ledge above a fireplace

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a coin on the shelf above the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is something handed over as security, so a deposit.

clue.text: Paul's crashed in automobile, to be brief

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a car is an automobile

indicators.note: crashed suggests the letters are smashed into a new order

parts.note: Paul and its S are used as written

explanation.surface: A short news report: Paul has had a car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' rearranges PAULS to PSULA; here the possessive's S counts as a letter, and 'to be' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsular means in compact, condensed form, as in a capsule summary, hence brief.

clue.text: Judge's anger follows start of untruths by politician

indicators.note: the word for anger comes after the other pieces
the start of untruths is its first letter

parts.note: MP stands for Member of Parliament
ire means anger

explanation.surface: A judge grows angry at a politician's lies.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire adjudicates a game or dispute, acting as its judge.

clue.text: Priest heads off singing a less modern hymn

indicators.note: the heads of the four words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A priest sets off singing an old-fashioned hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads off' could mean removing letters, but here it takes the heads of singing, a, less and modern.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song from the Book of Psalms, a kind of hymn.

clue.text: Help orchestral players to get burst of renewed energy

parts.note: to second someone is to support or help them
the wind section of an orchestra is its players of wind instruments

explanation.surface: An orchestra's woodwind section gets a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: A second wind is a fresh surge of strength after early tiredness.

clue.text: Enthusiastic prima donna returned

indicators.note: returned means the word is read back to front

parts.note: a prima donna is an opera's leading lady, a diva

explanation.surface: A keen opera star makes a comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or keen, a synonym of enthusiastic.

clue.text: Model's engaged to pretty person

indicators.note: the answer is held within the run of letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A fashion model is betrothed to a good-looking partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model's' is the definition plus 'is'; the answer spans the end of pretty and start of person.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a model or pattern, as in a prototype or classic example.

clue.text: Hearing aid could make mate erupt with rage, at first

indicators.note: could make says the letters can be made into something else
at first picks the first letter of rage

explanation.surface: A partner's old-fashioned hearing device sends them into a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges MATE, ERUPT and R.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear trumpet is an old horn-shaped device held to the ear to help hearing.
